nodes.name: Transfer_API
nodes.definition: Fund-transfer route: accepts a debit instruction from the mobile channel, posts it to the core ledger and returns a receipt.

nodes.name: Fund_Transfer_Process
nodes.definition: The business process a transfer must complete exactly once: authorise, debit, credit, notify and reconcile against one instruction id.

nodes.name: Idempotency_Token
nodes.definition: A client-supplied unique request id the server remembers for a TTL window, so a retried or replayed instruction executes once.

nodes.name: Signature_Verification
nodes.definition: A per-request signature over the business fields, checked server-side before the instruction is accepted.

nodes.name: Replay_Attack
nodes.definition: A captured instruction is re-sent unchanged and accepted a second time, because nothing marks the request as already seen.

nodes.name: Duplicate_Debit
nodes.definition: One customer intent produces two ledger postings: a timeout resend or a double tap debits the account twice.

nodes.name: Race_Condition
nodes.definition: Two concurrent submissions both read 'not yet processed' and both post, so the balance check passes twice.

nodes.name: Financial_Security_Level_3
nodes.definition: GB/T 22239 level-3 transaction-integrity clause: a funds instruction must execute once, and its acceptance must be traceable.

nodes.name: JR_T_0185_API_Spec
nodes.definition: JR/T 0185-2020 commercial-bank API security spec: a fund-moving API must resist replay and guarantee idempotency per instruction.
aliases: 商业银行应用程序接口安全管理规范

edges.evidence: Hand-authored benchmark: the route exists to serve exactly one process, and the process is what carries the 'exactly once' requirement.
Hand-authored benchmark: 'exactly once' is unreachable without a request identity the server can deduplicate on.
Hand-authored benchmark: the second required control - present on the route, so the reasoner must not fire on it.
Hand-authored benchmark: the review finding - the handler has no request-id table and no TTL window.
Hand-authored benchmark: read as 'the absence of this control permits this flaw' - the reasoner only crosses it when the control is missing.
Hand-authored benchmark: a retried timeout has no dedupe key, so the ledger posts twice.
Hand-authored benchmark: without a unique key the two concurrent posts cannot be serialised or collapsed.
Hand-authored benchmark: level 3 requires one execution per instruction; a replayed instruction executes twice.
Hand-authored benchmark: a second posting breaks the same transaction-integrity clause.
Hand-authored benchmark: the spec asks a fund-moving API to be idempotent per instruction; a race is the failure to be.
